units.title: Reproducible builds and supply chain
units.mappingEvidence: #54 ports SI-35 draft #45: .dockerignore excludes secrets/runtime data; Docker and CI install with npm ci against the committed package-lock.json. With #30/#31/#33/#34/#35 (digest-pinned images, SBOM/provenance release workflow, release-request dispatch, deployment-image verification) the supply-chain scope is implemented. Closed drafts #45-#49 are never counted.

units.title: Production deployment
units.mappingEvidence: Live Render service intake-pam (Docker, auto-deploy from main) runs migrations, one-time bootstrap and the worker beside the web app (scripts/container-start.sh, commit 079f733); /api/health and /api/ready verified live on 2026-11-17. #54 adds bounded readiness, stricter preflight and migration-target/deployment-image checks (from draft #47); #53 points the health probe at the live service.

units.title: Data protection and durability
externalPrerequisites: Owner: provide a private S3-compatible bucket; set DOCUMENT_STORAGE_DRIVER=s3, DOCUMENT_S3_ENDPOINT, DOCUMENT_S3_REGION, DOCUMENT_S3_BUCKET, DOCUMENT_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, DOCUMENT_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY on the service and the same names as repository secrets; run the Live provider verification workflow with require=s3.

Owner: provide a malware scanner (MALWARE_SCANNER_DRIVER=http with MALWARE_SCANNER_URL, MALWARE_SCANNER_PROVIDER, MALWARE_SCANNER_TOKEN; or clamscan with CLAMSCAN_DATABASE_DIR on an instance with at least 2 GB) and run the workflow with require=scanner.
Owner: set NEON_API_KEY and NEON_PROJECT_ID (optional NEON_SOURCE_BRANCH_ID, NEON_DATABASE_NAME, NEON_ROLE_NAME) as repository secrets and run the restore-drill job.
units.mappingEvidence: #54 (from draft #48): S3 create-only versions, no redirects, bounded timeouts, categorical scan failures. #55: retention sweep for drafts and idempotency responses, opt-in live S3/scanner verification and Neon point-in-time restore drill, operations runbook (key custody, restore). Live acceptance needs owner-provided provider credentials.

units.title: E2EESA aligned security architecture
units.mappingEvidence: #54 (from draft #49): undeclared/inherited answer keys dropped, canonical protected-payload and webhook-secret envelopes, categorical webhook failures. ADR 0036 reviews endpoint encryption, audited disclosure boundaries and achievable claims; security/e2eesa-inventory.json lists components and flows. The E2EESA status stages are tracked separately and stay unchecked; independent expert review is deferred by owner policy and is not claimed.

units.title: Notifications and downstream integration
externalPrerequisites: Owner: choose an email provider; set EMAIL_TRANSPORT_DRIVER=http, EMAIL_HTTP_URL, EMAIL_HTTP_TOKEN, EMAIL_FROM (optional EMAIL_PROVIDER) on the service and as repository secrets, plus LIVE_EMAIL_TEST_RECIPIENT as a repository secret; run the Live provider verification workflow with require=email.
units.mappingEvidence: #52 capability negotiation for downstream adapters; signed webhooks and event feed from #16/#21; #54 bounded retry backoff (from draft #46); #55 HTTPS email transport for notifications and correspondence, registered only when configured, verified with a local fake API on the real worker. Live email acceptance needs an owner-chosen provider.

units.title: Monitoring and production acceptance
externalPrerequisites: Owner: after providers are configured, run the synthetic end-to-end acceptance in docs/ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER.md on the live service and keep GitHub Actions failure notifications enabled for the health workflow.
units.mappingEvidence: #53/#55: scheduled read-only health monitor of the live service with a bounded cold-start wake phase (GitHub Actions failure notifications are the alert channel); readiness diagnostics (#38); deployment-image verification; rollback and incident procedures in docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md; acceptance ledger in docs/ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER.md.

units.title: Release security/usability/load tests
units.mappingEvidence: #55 adds concurrent-load and concurrent-idempotency tests plus retention, provider-gated delivery and throttle tests on real PostgreSQL with the served app and the real worker. Existing evidence: adversarial tenancy/authorization tests, axe accessibility in a real browser, keyboard-only journeys, worker lease recovery and clamscan scanning in the CI end-to-end suite.

units.title: Stable generic 1.0 release
externalPrerequisites: Owner: decide to release 1.0.0; then one PR changes package.json version and release-request.json (immutable source SHA), and the downstream verifier adds 1.0.0 to supportedVersions before the deployment reports it.
units.mappingEvidence: Acceptance ledger (docs/ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER.md), support runbook (docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md) and downstream compatibility notes. Cutting the stable 1.0.0 release is an owner decision coordinated with the downstream identity verifier's supportedVersions.
